identity.name: Quiet Current
identity.descriptor: Editorial sound and audio post-production studio
identity.origin: The fictional riverside district of Bellweather
identity.nameMeaning: A current can carry a story without announcing itself; quiet names the space left for human attention.

essence.oneLine: Quiet Current shapes documentary and spoken-word sound without polishing away the room it came from.
essence.promise: Speech stays intelligible, place stays present and every edit has a reason.
essence.tension: Deep night colour and luminous waveform signals held inside calm editorial whitespace.

worldview.belief: Good sound does not call attention to processing; it helps a listener notice voice, place and silence.
worldview.future: Documentary and spoken-word work treats listening, accessibility and sonic consent as part of editorial craft.
worldview.humanRole: Editors make narrative judgements, listen with contributors and decide what a silence means.
worldview.technologyRole: Tools reveal, repair and organise audio while editorial responsibility stays with people.
politicalOrSocialBoundaries: Do not turn the brand into a party-political position.
Do not use anxiety, shame or social status as sales pressure.
Do not romanticise labour or hide who performs it.

purpose.why: Stories need sonic clarity without losing the air, distance and texture that make them true to their setting.
purpose.mission: Edit, mix and document spoken-word sound with restraint and a clear editorial trail.
purpose.vision: Careful listening becomes a visible, shareable part of how audio stories are made.

positioning.category: Editorial sound, dialogue editing and audio post-production
positioning.audience: Independent documentary teams, narrative podcasts and cultural producers
positioning.need: Clear, emotionally honest sound with a workflow that non-audio collaborators can review.
positioning.difference: Every mix includes a plain-language listening map that explains the role of voice, place, music and silence.
proof: Each fictional delivery includes a timestamped listening map.
The fictional review method separates intelligibility, editorial change and technical repair.
positioning.pricePosition: Project-priced by material length, editorial complexity, restoration needs and delivery versions.

offers.name: Dialogue and place
offers.job: Make speech intelligible while preserving a believable sense of room and location.
offers.outcome: The team receives a clean editorial mix, stems and a listening map.

offers.name: Series sound system
offers.job: Give recurring episodes a coherent voice, music, loudness and review pattern.
offers.outcome: Editors work from reusable session, cue and delivery rules.

audiences.name: Documentary editor
audiences.context: Picture and story are moving, while location recordings vary widely.
audiences.job: Hear what can be repaired, what should remain and where editorial choices were made.
audiences.desiredShift: From handing sound over as a black box to making informed listening decisions.
audiences.language: Use timestamps, audible consequences and plain comparisons.

audiences.name: Narrative series producer
audiences.context: Several episodes, editors and remote recordings need one coherent listening experience.
audiences.job: Keep voice, music and delivery consistent without flattening each story.
audiences.desiredShift: From episode-by-episode rescue to a repeatable sound system.
audiences.language: Editorial structure first, technical specification second.

values.name: Listen before cleaning
values.meaning: Noise can be a problem, a place or a piece of evidence.

values.name: Silence has a job
values.meaning: Absence can carry thought, discomfort or transition.
behaviours: remove gaps only with editorial reason

values.name: Review stays human
values.meaning: Collaborators should understand and hear every important decision.

messaging.masterMessage: Let the voice arrive clearly. Keep enough room around it to believe where it came from.

messagePillars.name: Place
messagePillars.claim: Useful room and location remain audible.

messagePillars.name: Reason
messagePillars.claim: Major edits are explained in plain language.

messaging.storyPattern: Begin with one sound the listener should notice. Reveal what obscures it. Show the editorial choice. End with the space that remains.

dimensions.instruction: Describe what can be heard before stating what should change.
Lead with story effect; give the technical method after it.
Keep natural cadence and avoid luxury-studio language.

avoid: claims with no physical or recorded proof

do: give an owner and next update
say what happened and what remains safe
avoid: jokes during loss or payment issues

language.defaultRegister: Clear editorial English. Quiet confidence, no studio mystique and no treating collaborators as technically naive.
language.sentenceRhythm: Measured sentences with deliberate space. A short sentence may stand alone when the pause is part of the thought.

terminology.cleanup: dialogue repair or noise reduction with named consequence
terminology.silence: pause, gap or room tone by its actual role
terminology.AI: name the specific tool and retained human decision

formatting: lists only when they improve scanning
language.inclusiveLanguage: Name real roles and actions. Do not invent personal characteristics or reduce an audience to a demographic stereotype.

allowed: This fictional mix follows the stated delivery specification.

forbidden: a certification that does not exist

concept.direction: Midnight violet, fog-white editorial space and a coral current line that appears only where listening changes.
concept.rationale: The system gives silence visible space and treats waveforms as evidence, not decoration.
concept.visualTension: Dark acoustic depth and pale paper; continuous audio and sharply edited margins.

usage: Midnight and fog carry most surfaces.
Coral marks an editorial intervention, never generic energy.
Meter green appears only after a named check passes.

gradients.name: Room falloff
gradients.job: Slow atmospheric depth behind an isolated listening object

rules: Set timestamps and version names in mono.
Never stretch type into a fake waveform.

logo.idea: Two quiet parallel lines joined by one shallow current bend; the gap is as important as the stroke.
logo.clearspace: At least the cap height of the first letter on every side.
placement: align to the primary content grid
keep away from photography focal points
use one-colour variants when contrast is uncertain
dont: use the symbol as a decorative texture

layout.principle: Editorial margins act as silence; a single current line connects related moments without filling the page.
layout.grid: Eight columns on desktop, four on tablet and one generous reading column on mobile.
layout.density: Low around narrative and listening prompts; compact only in timestamps and delivery lists.
composition: align timestamps to a stable rail
use one current line per view
pair waveform detail with plain-language note
let still images hold longer than expected
responsive: keep the primary action above bottom navigation
allow text to wrap without collision
prove zero horizontal overflow at 390 px

shapes.geometry: Long rails, shallow arcs, timestamp ticks and open-ended frames.
shapes.corners: 6 px for controls, square frames for evidence, fully rounded only for playheads.
shapes.strokes: 1 px rails and waveforms, 2 px icons, 3 px active current.

iconography.job: Identify listening, edit, comment, version and delivery actions without borrowing consumer-player decoration.
iconography.metaphor: Editorial marks and simple acoustic relationships drawn with open lines.
iconography.grid: 24 × 24 px with a 2 px optical safe area.
iconography.stroke: 1.75 px with round joins and open terminals.
iconography.detail: One primary form and no more than one supporting detail; test at 16 px.
iconography.color: One colour by default; current coral marks only an active or selected state.
opticalRules: open narrow gaps at small sizes
align repeated elements to whole pixels where possible
dont: put the icon in a presentation mockup

illustration.job: Explain voice, place, music and silence as separate but related listening layers.
illustration.style: Sparse editorial diagrams with translucent bands and one coral edit mark.
illustration.perspective: Flat timeline or sectional listening map.
dont: cute characters without a narrative job

photography.job: Show the concentration, place and small physical gestures behind listening and editorial sound.
subjects: a contributor in a real recording context
room details that remain audible in the story
environment: quiet edit room with ordinary equipment
desk with notes and version marks
photography.moment: The pause before a decision: listening back, marking a time, or asking to hear it once more.
composition: screen content unreadable or replaced with approved real UI
negative space on the listening side
photography.camera: Locked or gently handheld at seated height; movement should feel like breathing, not coverage.
photography.lens: 40-65 mm natural perspective; shallow only enough to isolate attention.
photography.light: Soft side light with monitor spill kept subtle; preserve dark detail.
photography.palette: Midnight shadows, fog paper, skin kept natural and a single coral object or edit mark.
photography.grade: Low saturation, open shadows, quiet warm skin and cool room separation.
photography.texture: Paper notes, acoustic cloth, worn controls and room surfaces remain believable.
do: grade a series as one shoot

motion.principle: Movement follows listening: arrive, hold, mark, compare and release.
signature: a current line pausing at an edit
a timestamp resolving after playback stops
two versions crossfading without a flash
motion.reducedMotion: Replace spatial movement and looping signals with an immediate static state change.
avoid: motion that competes with the task

dataVisualization.principle: Waveform, loudness and version data must support an audible editorial decision, not imply scientific certainty.
dataVisualization.colors: Fog and midnight as base, lavender for selection, coral for change, meter green only for a passed named check.
rules: never use colour as the only distinction

representation.principle: Show contributors, editors and producers as people with editorial agency; listening is an action, not passive ambience.

casting.people: Usually one listener or a two-person review; larger groups only when collaboration is the actual subject.
casting.age: Adults across realistic editorial roles and career stages.
casting.gender: Do not code technical control, sensitivity or authority through gender.
casting.ethnicity: Choose series casting deliberately and never infer contributor identity from recordings or names.
casting.ability: Include varied ways of listening and communicating when relevant, with authentic input rather than inspiration framing.
casting.roles: The contributor retains ownership of their words; the editor is shown making accountable choices.
casting.wardrobe: Quiet ordinary clothing suited to the actual room or location, without creative-industry costume.
casting.behaviour: Listening, marking, explaining, recording or sitting with a pause; no headphone dance.

representation.sensitiveAttributePolicy: Never infer ethnicity, religion, health, sexual orientation, gender identity or another sensitive attribute from a name, face, place or industry. Unknown remains unknown.
representation.consent: Recognisable real people require documented permission for the exact channel and context. Do not reuse customer or staff imagery as generic campaign material.
avoid: roles assigned through gender or age stereotypes
synthetic faces presented as real staff
children without a necessary context and explicit guardian consent

sensory.sonicIdentity: Near-field clarity with preserved room, short coral edit signals and silence treated as an active layer.

music.rhythm: sparse and asymmetrical with long rests
music.harmony: open intervals, gentle tension, no automatic emotional resolution

voiceover.voice: Natural adult voice appropriate to the story; no default prestige accent.
voiceover.delivery: Close, thoughtful and unperformed, with complete breaths and meaningful pauses.

soundEffects.role: Mark editorial state without entering the story world as decoration.

sensory.silence: Silence is authored. Protect it before testimony, after difficult material and wherever a listener needs time rather than instruction.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA for digital work; accessible PDF practices for documents.
contrast: Normal text must reach at least 4.5:1.
Large text and interface boundaries must reach at least 3:1.
Colour can never be the only carrier of state.
Use only pairings that have been measured, not guessed from appearance.
motion: Do not autoplay essential information without controls.
Every animated state needs an immediate static equivalent.
text: Keep body copy as selectable, scalable text.
Write links that describe their destination.
Explain specialist terms at first use.
media: Alt text describes the image's communication job.
Decorative images receive empty alt text.
Video includes captions and a transcript.

trademarks: The name is fictional but still requires a real clearance search before commercial adoption.
Never recreate a third-party mark in generated assets.
assets: Record the source and licence for every font, image, icon and sound.
Keep logo masters as vectors outside image-generation prompts.
Do not copy imagery from an unrelated real organisation into this example.
claims: Every public claim needs a real source or owner approval.
Fictional proof cannot be reused as a real testimonial.
Measure environmental, time and performance claims before stating them.
privacy: Do not add personal data that is unnecessary for the artifact.
Use recognisable people only with documented rights.
